newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa dips to new lows, correction expected.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa dips to new lows, correction expected.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures drifted down to fresh seven-month lows, but Tuesday's performance appeared to confirm the market's tendency to consolidate technically oversold levels, traders said.
"It's running a risk of short-covering. It could bounce up anytime," said one trader, adding there was a significant number of shorts in the market.
Losses on the key March contract stalled at the 930 stg level on Tuesday and the position ended at 932 stg, down four stg on the day. Front-month December shed five stg to end at 899.
Turnover totalled a healthy 7,755 lots, which mostly featured two-way activity around the March structure and outright selling on December.
Traders said New York's failure to make its opening due pressured London through arbitrage sales, but sterling's drift off the day's fresh highs provided some support.
The structure was widening with Dec/March trading at 33-34 stg as nearby supplies looked secure.
Physical news was slack with some 90,000 tonnes of cocoa still piled up in Abidjan pending a decision on freight rates and export licences.
Brokers GNI said in its monthly commodity review that the world stock-to-consumption ratio could be lower than previously imagined.
Recent upward revisions to the world stockpile may have been exaggerated because of the deluge of cocoa piling into Rotterdam this year to profit from the September squeeze.
"However, it could be another six months or so before this has a positive effect on prices. Short-term, the outlook is bleak," GNI concluded.

The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) pegged the stock/consumption ratio at 51.7 percent at the end of 1995/96. On the charts, support on March is expected to hold around 925 stg and resistance is pegged at 955.
